Point update-ийг range-ийн элемент бүрт хийхэд $O(n\log n)$ хүрнэ. Difference array нь бүх update-ийн дараах final array-д сайн, харин дунд нь sum query хэрэгтэй бол хангалтгүй.
Node бүхэлдээ update-д багтвал sum-д $x(r-l+1)$ нэмээд lazy-д $x$ хадгална. Child руу орох хэрэг гарвал push хийн тэдний sum, tag-ийг шинэчилнэ; parent-ийн lazy-г $0$ болгоно.

Point update-ийг range-ийн бүх index-д давтвал урт range бүр $O(n\log n)$ болно. Lazy propagation нь бүтэн node interval-д ижил addition ирэхэд leaf бүр рүү тэр даруй орохгүй. Sum нь interval length-ээр үржүүлсэн addition-аар шууд шинэчлэгдэнэ.

$tree[v]$ нь тухайн interval-ийн одоогийн зөв sum. $lazy[v]$ нь тэр sum-д аль хэдийн орсон, харин хүүхдүүдэд хараахан дамжуулаагүй нэг элементэд нэмэх утга. Иймээс apply дээр $tree[v]+=x(r-l+1)$ ба $lazy[v]+=x$; node өөрөө update хүлээж байгаа гэсэн үг биш.

Хэсэгчлэн query/update хийхэд хүүхдүүдийн утга хэрэгтэй болно. Тэгэхэд push нь pending addition-ийг хоёр хүүхэд дээр apply хийгээд parent tag-ийг $0$ болгоно. Бүрэн багтсан query дээр sum бэлэн тул push хэрэггүй. Хоёр addition-ийн composition нь sum; assignment update бол ийм composition биш.

en.title: Lazy segment trees — deferring range additions
en.summary: Extend the recursive sum tree with range addition and explain exactly what each lazy tag means.

blocks.text: Start with $a=[2,1,3,4]$. Adding $5$ everywhere produces $[7,6,8,9]$ with sum $30$. Must we visit all four leaves for this one update?

sections.title: 2. From the simple approach to the new idea

blocks.text: Updating every point separately can cost $O(n\log n)$. Difference arrays suit final reconstruction, but not interleaved sum queries.
For full coverage, add $x(r-l+1)$ to the sum and $x$ to the lazy tag. Before descending, push this addition into both children’s sums and tags, then clear the parent tag.

Updating every point in a range separately may cost $O(n\log n)$. Lazy propagation avoids visiting each leaf when an addition covers a whole node interval. Update its sum immediately by multiplying the addition by the interval length.

$tree[v]$ is the current correct sum of its interval. $lazy[v]$ is an increment already included in that sum but not yet passed to its children. Thus apply adds $x(r-l+1)$ to the sum and $x$ to the tag; the node itself is not waiting to be updated.

A partial query or update needs child values. Push applies the pending addition to both children and clears the parent tag. A fully covered query uses the already-correct sum without pushing. Addition tags compose by summing; assignment tags need different composition rules.

items: $\mathrm{tree}[v]$ is the current correct sum for the node’s interval.
$\mathrm{lazy}[v]$ is a per-element addition not yet sent to children. It is already included in tree($v$).
Apply updates the sum and tag; push transfers a tag to children.

blocks.text: Follow this detailed trace slowly. At each step, identify which stored value changes and why.

rows: For $a=[2,1,3,4]$, the root sum is $10$. Query $[0,3]$ returns it directly.
Add $5$ on $[1,2]$: the two leaf values become $6,8$, and their parent sums become $8,12$.
The root sum becomes $20$. Query $[1,2]$ gives $6+8=14$.
To see deferred work, now add $3$ to the full range: root sum becomes $20+3\cdot4=32$, root tag becomes $3$, and the children stay unchanged.
A later $[0,1]$ query pushes at the root. The left sum becomes $8+3\cdot2=14$, the right $12+3\cdot2=18$, and the root tag clears to $0$.

items: For no overlap, do nothing or return zero.
For full coverage, apply the update or return the stored sum.
For partial coverage, push before recursive calls.
After updates, recompute the parent from its children.

sections.title: 6. C++17 code and how to read it

blocks.text: LazySeg st($a$) supports st.add($l,r,x$) and st.query($l,r$) with inclusive bounds, matching the plain recursive tree. Its lazy tags represent addition, not assignment.
Read apply first: increasing every element by $x$ increases the total by interval length times $x$. Push applies the same rule separately to each child.
Require valid ranges and sums and length-times-increment products fitting long long. Empty-range updates do nothing and queries return zero.

items: Apply multiplies by length for the sum but not for lazy, whose tag is a per-element addition.
Push stops at leaves because they have no children, and does nothing for a zero tag.
After a partial update, recombine the updated child sums. Query is not const because pushing changes the internal representation.

blocks.text: Section 13 contains a complete runnable program with the same implementation, input format and checked sample output.

sections.title: 7. Why is it correct and how fast is it?

blocks.text: Every stored node sum is correct, though children may still await a parent’s addition. Push transfers that addition exactly once and clears the tag, allowing partial queries to read correct child information.
Build is $O(n)$; range additions and queries are $O(\log n)$; space is $O(n)$. Full coverage stops descent instead of visiting every leaf.

items: Do not add a lazy value to the node sum again: apply already included it.
Clear the parent tag after push or it will be applied repeatedly.
Addition tags cannot be reused unchanged for assignment updates.

blocks.text: In the original example, apply add($1,2,3$). What are the array and total?
Check your answer: $[2,4,6,4]$, total $16$.
blocks.label: Show answer

blocks.text: Add $2$, then $3$ to the entire root interval. What is lazy?
Check your answer: $5$: addition tags compose by addition.
blocks.label: Show answer

blocks.text: Once you can trace the example without looking at the code, write the implementation yourself. Compare it with a simple loop on new inputs. The links offer another explanation; this lesson’s prose, examples and code were written for Erdene Club.

sections.title: 11. Why does it take this amount of time?

blocks.text: A range addition does not descend to every leaf. A fully covered node adds $x(r-l+1)$ to its sum, records $x$ in its lazy tag and stops. Deferring changes to all descendants is the main saving.

On partial coverage, push updates only the two immediate children’s sums and tags in $O(1)$ work, not their entire subtrees. Both range queries and updates descend further only at the at-most-two partial boundary nodes per level. With $O(\log n)$ levels, each operation costs $O(\log n)$. Build visits the $2n-1$ nodes once: $O(n)$.
Example: adding $5$ to all $1024$ elements only changes the root sum and tag. A later small-range query pushes tags only along the necessary paths, rather than first updating all $1024$ leaves.
This applies to range addition and sum, whose apply/push operations take constant work. It does not mean every type of range update can use one lazy tag with this bound.

blocks.text: How many times does $4$ occur in $a=[2,4,4,7,9]$? Finding the two boundaries lets us count without revisiting all equal elements. A boundary is a position and may equal the end sentinel $n$.

sections.title: 2. From the direct approach to the insight

blocks.text: A direct scan takes $O(n)$ per query. On sorted input use the predicate $a_i\gex$. It changes from false to true at most once, enabling binary search.
Lower bound is the first boundary at which $x$ could appear; upper bound is the boundary after all equal values. One comparison sign changes the meaning of positions and frequency counts.
For $x=4$, lower bound is $1$ and upper bound is $3$, giving frequency $3-1=2$. For absent $x=5$, both boundaries are $3$ and the frequency is correctly zero.
For $x=10$ both answers are $5=n$. This correctly says every value is below $10$; it is not a valid element index to dereference.

items: Initialize $l=0$, $r=n$. An empty array ends immediately.
While $l<r$, compute $mid=l+(r-l)/2$.
If $a_{mid}\gex$, set $r=mid$; otherwise set $l=mid+1$.
Return $l$. Subtract lower bound from upper bound to count equal values.

blocks.text: Maintain that indices before $l$ fail the predicate and valid indices at or beyond $r$ satisfy it. A true middle remains a possible answer; a false middle is discarded with the preceding false region.
The width decreases until $l=r$, leaving a unique boundary. Exactly the positions from lower bound up to upper bound contain $x$, so their difference is the frequency.

en.title: Sliding window — moving a window without backtracking
en.summary: Use positive-array range sums to see why two nested loops can still be linear.

blocks.text: Find the longest contiguous subarray of $a$ with sum at most $K$. There are $O(n^2)$ intervals. Prefix sums make each sum query fast but do not reduce the number of intervals being considered.

sections.title: 2. From the direct approach to the insight

blocks.text: Positivity is the crucial assumption. Extending the right boundary cannot reduce the sum, and removing the leftmost element cannot increase it. If the sum exceeds $K$, move the left boundary forward until the window becomes valid.
A discarded left boundary cannot become useful at a later right boundary: only positive values are being added. Continue from the previous left boundary instead of restarting the search.
For $a=[2,1,4,2,3,1]$ and $K=7$, the first three values sum to $7$ and have length $3$. Adding the next $2$ produces $9$; removing the leading $2$ leaves valid window $[1,4,2]$.
Adding $3$ produces sum $10$. Remove $1$ and then $4$, leaving $[2,3]$. The final $1$ makes $[2,3,1]$ of length $3$, so the best length remains $3$.

items: Initialize $l=0$, $sum=0$, $ans=0$.
Move $r$ from left to right and add $a_r$ to the sum.
While $sum>K$, remove $a_l$ and increment $l$.
Update the best answer using the valid length $r-l+1$.

blocks.text: At the end of an iteration, the stored sum matches the current window and is at most $K$. Every discarded starting position made the window too large at this right boundary, so none can produce a valid interval ending here.

The smallest remaining $l$ yields the longest valid interval for this $r$. Considering every right boundary therefore finds the global maximum. With $K=0$, positive elements are removed and the valid empty length is zero.

sections.title: 6. Where the running time comes from

blocks.text: The outer loop runs $n$ times. The inner while can increment $l$ at most $n$ times over the entire run because it never moves backward. Each value is added once and removed at most once, giving $O(n)$ total time.
The search state uses $O(1)$ extra space; storing the input costs $O(n)$. One individual iteration can remove many values, but the aggregate work is linear: an example of amortized analysis.

items: Use long long for $sum$: summing $2\cdot10^5$ values of $10^9$ overflows int.
$l$ marks the first window position and $r$ the most recently added index.
Compute the length after the while, when the window has become valid.
$ans=0$ handles the case where no nonempty interval qualifies.

sections.title: 2. From the direct approach to the insight

blocks.text: A traversal reaches every vertex in its starting component. Starting again at an unvisited vertex does not repeat the same work: it explores a group unreachable from the previous starts.
Assign a neighbour the colour $1-color_v$. An already coloured neighbour with the same colour is a contradiction. Start another BFS from each uncoloured vertex.
The path $1-2-3$ and separate edge $4-5$ form two components. BFS from $1$ reaches only $1,2,3$; the outer loop must start another traversal at $4$.

items: Insert each undirected edge in both adjacency lists.

blocks.text: Every enqueued vertex is reachable from the start: either it is the start itself or a neighbour of a previously reached vertex. Thus a traversal never mixes separate components.

If a reachable vertex remained unvisited, consider the first unvisited vertex on a path from the start. Processing its visited predecessor would have enqueued it, a contradiction. The entire component is therefore visited.

For colouring, fixing the start colour fixes others through path parity. An equal-colour edge contradicts those constraints. If no conflict appears, every edge has opposite-coloured endpoints, so the produced colouring is valid.

en.title: Interval DP — reason from the final operation
en.summary: Derive interval states, split transitions and dependency order from adjacent merges.

blocks.text: There are $n$ weighted items in a row. Merging adjacent groups costs their combined weight. Find the minimum total cost to obtain one group. Branching over the first merge creates many choices and repeats the same residual problems.

sections.title: 2. From the direct approach to the insight

blocks.text: Consider the final merge instead of the first. Just before $a[l..r]$ becomes one group, it consists of adjacent groups $[l,k]$ and $[k+1,r]$. Every valid merge sequence has such a final split.

Let $dp_{l,r}$ be the minimum cost to combine $[l,r]$. The final merge always costs the total interval weight, independent of the split. Therefore $dp_{l,r}=\min_{l\le k<r}(dp_{l,k}+dp_{k+1,r}+S(l,r))$.
For $[10,20,30,40]$, first merge $10,20$ for cost $30$, then $30,30$ for cost $60$, then $60,40$ for cost $100$, totalling $190$.
For $[10,20,30]$, the final split is either $10\mid20,30$, costing $0+50+60=110$, or $10,20\mid30$, costing $30+0+60=90$. The interval optimum is $90$.

items: Set $dp_{i,i}=0$: one item requires no merge.
Build prefix sums so $S(l,r)=prefix_{r+1}-prefix_l$ is available in $O(1)$.
Process interval lengths from $2$ through $n$.

Print $dp_{0,n-1}$.

blocks.text: Induct on interval length. Length one correctly costs zero. The final merge of any longer interval combines two shorter intervals whose optima are available by induction.

If either child interval uses a nonoptimal merge sequence, replacing it with a cheaper one does not change the final combined weight. Thus an optimum appears among the transitions. Conversely, every transition constructs a valid merge sequence, proving the minimum is exact.

sections.title: 6. Where the running time comes from

blocks.text: There are $O(n^2)$ intervals and up to $O(n)$ splits per interval, giving $O(n^3)$ worst-case time. Recomputing interval sums inside transitions can make it even slower. The name DP does not imply quadratic time.

The DP table uses $O(n^2)$ space and prefix sums use $O(n)$. Cubic work may fit around $n=400$, but not at $n=2\cdot10^5$. Special recurrences admit optimizations such as Knuth optimization, whose assumptions must be proved rather than guessed.

items: $dp[l][r]$ uses a closed interval; its prefix-sum right index is $r+1$.

en.title: Tree DP — combining child-subtree answers
en.summary: Count independent sets using two states and see how a parent choice restricts its children.

blocks.text: Each tree vertex may be selected or not, but both endpoints of an edge cannot be selected. Count these independent sets. Enumerating all $2^n$ subsets is too slow for a large tree.

sections.title: 2. From the direct approach to the insight

blocks.text: After rooting the tree, different child subtrees have no edges between them. They become independent once the parent choice is fixed. One count per subtree is insufficient because children need to know whether their parent is selected.

Let $white_v$ count sets excluding $v$ and $black_v$ count sets including it. Over children $u$, use $white_v=\prod_u(white_u+black_u)$ and $black_v=\prod_u white_u$. Multiply independent child choices, but add the two alternatives for a single child.
Vertex $1$ has leaf children $2,3$. Each leaf has white and black counts of $1$. Excluding the root gives $(1+1)(1+1)=4$; including it gives $1\cdot1=1$, for a total of $5$.
Including the root permits only $\{1\}$. Excluding it permits the empty set, $\{2\}$, $\{3\}$ and $\{2,3\}$. Listing these explicitly checks the meaning of the transition.

items: Root at vertex $0$ and construct parents and an order in which parents precede children.
Process the order in reverse so every child is solved before its parent.
Initialize both counts to $1$ and multiply the available choices from each child.
Add the root white and black counts modulo the modulus.

blocks.text: A leaf has one set including it and one excluding it. Assume child subtrees have been counted correctly. Selecting $v$ requires every child root to be excluded; excluding $v$ permits either child state.

Different child subtrees have no connecting edges, so combining their valid choices creates no new conflict. Every valid set corresponds to exactly one such combination, justifying multiplication. Induction yields the final root sum.

sections.title: 6. Where the running time comes from

blocks.text: Each traversal examines both directions of each edge, and each child contributes constant arithmetic to the DP. Total time is $O(n)$; two states per vertex do not enumerate $2^n$ subsets.
Adjacency lists, parents, traversal order and the two DP arrays use $O(n)$ space. Explicit ordering avoids recursive DFS stack overflow on a path of $n=2\cdot10^5$ vertices.

en.title: Bellman–Ford — negative edges and relaxation
en.summary: Relax all edges when Dijkstra assumptions fail, and detect reachable negative cycles.

blocks.text: With negative edges, the apparently closest vertex may improve later. If $1\to2$ has weight $2$, $1\to3$ has weight $5$, and $3\to2$ has weight $-10$, the true distance to vertex $2$ is $-5$. Dijkstra's greedy proof does not extend to negative weights.

sections.title: 2. From the direct approach to the insight

blocks.text: For edge $u\to v$ of weight $w$, append the edge to a known path to $u$ to obtain candidate $dist_u+w$. Replacing $dist_v$ when this is smaller is called relaxation.

One pass may process edges before their dependencies are known. Repeated full passes propagate information along paths. Without a relevant negative cycle, a shortest path can be made simple and uses at most $n-1$ edges.
For edges $1\to2$ of weight $4$, $1\to3$ of weight $5$, $2\to3$ of weight $-2$, and $3\to4$ of weight $3$, start with $dist=[0,INF,INF,INF]$. Relaxations eventually produce $[0,4,2,5]$.
Changing the input edge order changes how many distances propagate in one pass, but enough full passes produce the same final shortest distances.

items: Set $dist_0=0$ and all other distances to INF.
Relax every edge for at most $n$ full passes.
Do not add a weight to INF when $u$ is unreachable.
Stop if a pass changes nothing. A change in the $n$th pass indicates a reachable negative cycle.

blocks.text: Every finite stored distance is the cost of a real walk: the initial zero is the empty path, and each relaxation appends a real edge. The algorithm cannot invent an unrealistically short walk.

After $k$ passes, candidates for all paths of at most $k$ edges have propagated. In-place updates may also use longer walks during one pass, so the invariant is not exactly $k$ edges. Without a reachable negative cycle, a simple shortest path uses at most $n-1$ edges, by which time all distances are correct.

An improvement after that point implies a negative cycle in the improving walk. An unreachable cycle cannot pass the INF guard. Detecting a cycle anywhere instead requires a virtual source, or equivalently initializing every distance to zero.

sections.title: 6. Where the running time comes from

blocks.text: Each pass examines $m$ edges and there are at most $n$ passes, giving $O(nm)$ worst-case time. Early stopping helps some instances but does not change the worst-case bound.

The edge list uses $O(m)$ space and distances use $O(n)$. This direct method does not fit when both $n,m$ are $2\cdot10^5$. Inspect additional structure, such as the absence of negative edges or a DAG, before choosing an algorithm.

blocks.text: Замын жин сөрөг байж болох үед хамгийн ойр харагдсан оройг дахин сайжрахгүй гэж үзэж болохгүй. Жишээ нь $1\to2$ жин $2$, $1\to3$ жин $5$, $3\to2$ жин $-10$ бол орой $2$-ын зөв зай $-5$. Dijkstra-ийн greedy баталгаа сөрөг edge дээр үйлчлэхгүй.
Edge $u\to v$ жин $w$ байвал $u$ хүртэл мэдэж байгаа замын араас энэ edge-ийг залгаж $dist_u+w$ гэсэн шинэ candidate гаргана. Үүнийг одоогийн $dist_v$-ээс бага үед солихыг relaxation гэдэг.

Edge-үүдийг нэг удаа үзэхэд хүссэн dependency order бэлэн биш байж болно. Бүх edge-ийг дахин дахин үзвэл мэдээлэл зам дагуу тархана. Negative cycle байхгүй shortest path-ийг энгийн болгож болох тул хамгийн ихдээ $n-1$ edge хэрэгтэй.
$1\to2$ жин $4$, $1\to3$ жин $5$, $2\to3$ жин $-2$, $3\to4$ жин $3$. Эхэнд $dist=[0,INF,INF,INF]$. Relaxation-уудын дараа $[0,4,2,5]$ болно.

tutorials.title: String hashing — substring-ийн fingerprint
tutorials.summary: Prefix hash-аас substring-ийг хурдан харьцуулж, collision яагаад боломжтой хэвээр байдгийг ойлгоё.
tutorials.aliases: string-hashing String hashing — substring-ийн fingerprint String hashing — substring fingerprints

en.title: String hashing — substring fingerprints
en.summary: Compare substrings through prefix hashes while keeping collision limits explicit.

blocks.text: We repeatedly compare two substrings of one string. Comparing characters directly may cost $O(n)$ per query. We want a fixed-size fingerprint instead of inspecting the entire substring each time.

sections.title: 2. From the direct approach to the insight

blocks.text: Map letters to numbers $1..26$ and build prefix hashes $h_{i+1}=(h_iB+c_i)\bmod M$. Different powers retain order information; simply summing character values cannot distinguish ab from ba.
The hash of substring $[l,r)$ is $(h_r-h_lB^{r-l})\bmod M$. Subtraction removes the earlier prefix after aligning its powers. Substrings with different lengths can be rejected immediately.

In ababa, substrings $[0,3)$ and $[2,5)$ are both aba. Their normalized hashes match despite different positions. Substrings $[0,2)$ and $[1,3)$ are ab and ba, so their different order is represented in the polynomial fingerprint.

items: Build prefix hashes and powers $B^i$ for two moduli.
Convert a one-based closed input range $[l,r]$ to zero-based half-open $[l-1,r)$.
Check equal lengths, then compare the pair of hashes.
Keep fingerprint equality distinct from guaranteed string equality.

blocks.text: Expanding the recurrence expresses $h_r$ as the residue of $c_0B^{r-1}+\cdots+c_{r-1}$. The term $h_lB^{r-l}$ has exactly the powers of the first $l$ characters, so subtraction leaves the substring polynomial.

Equal substrings always have equal hashes, but different strings may collide after reduction. Infinitely many strings map to a finite range. Two moduli reduce collisions without eliminating them. A fixed base does not justify a universal probability guarantee against adversarial input.

sections.title: 6. Where the running time comes from

blocks.text: Prefix hashes and powers take constant work per character, hence $O(n)$. Each query uses constant arithmetic, giving $O(1)$ per query and $O(n+q)$ overall. Two moduli add a constant factor rather than changing the asymptotic bound.
Two prefix and two power vectors use $O(n)$ space. Calling substr per query would add an $O(length)$ copy even though fingerprint extraction itself is constant time.

items: MOD1, MOD2 and BASE are fingerprint parameters; long long holds intermediate products.
$p_i=B^i\bmod M$ and $h_i$ hashes the first $i$ characters.
Adding MOD before the final remainder normalizes a negative subtraction.
YES in this program means the two fingerprints match; choose an exact method such as KMP when a guaranteed proof is required.

blocks.text: A lowercase string of length $1\le n\le2\cdot10^5$ and $q$ valid one-based closed-range queries $l_1,r_1,l_2,r_2$. YES means matching fingerprints; NO guarantees different substrings.

items: Treating equal fingerprints as guaranteed equal strings.
Ignoring lengths or confusing $l$ and $l-1$ in prefix indices.
Failing to normalize negative residues or multiplying with int and overflowing.

blocks.text: For deterministic correctness, hashing can act as a preliminary filter, but verifying YES results character by character increases worst-case time. Compare it with exact linear methods such as KMP for String Matching.

How many possible fingerprint pairs exist?

blocks.text: No. There are only finitely many pairs, so distinct strings can still share one.
blocks.label: Show explanation

blocks.text: Нэг string-ийн хоёр substring ижил эсэхийг олон удаа шалгая. Бүрд нь тэмдэгтээр нь харьцуулбал нэг query $O(n)$ хүрч болно. Бид бүтэн substring-ийн оронд тогтмол хэмжээтэй fingerprint тооцохыг хүснэ.

Тэмдэгтүүдийг $1..26$ тоогоор орлуулж, $h_{i+1}=(h_i B+c_i)\bmod M$ prefix hash байгуул. Энд байрлал бүр өөр зэрэгтэй тул дарааллын мэдээлэл хадгална. Энгийн тэмдэгтийн нийлбэр бол ab, ba хоёрыг ялгахгүй.
$[l,r)$ substring-ийн hash нь $(h_r-h_lB^{r-l})\bmod M$. Prefix-ийн эхний хэсгийг яг ижил зэрэгт шилжүүлж хасаж байгаа нь энэ томьёоны шалтгаан. Урт нь ялгаатай хоёр substring-ийг шууд өөр гэж шийд.

ababa string-ийн $[0,3)$ болон $[2,5)$ нь хоёулаа aba. Prefix байрлал нь өөр боловч нормчилсон substring hash ижил гарна. Харин $[0,2)$ нь ab, $[1,3)$ нь ba тул дарааллын ялгаа hash-д тусах боломжтой.

items: Хоёр modulo-д prefix hash болон $B^i$ хүснэгт байгуул.
Input-ийн $1$-ээс эхэлсэн хаалттай $[l,r]$-г $0$-ээс эхэлсэн $[l-1,r)$ болгож хөрвүүл.
Урт тэнцүү эсэхийг шалгаад хоёр hash-ийн pair-ийг харьцуул.
Ижил fingerprint гэдэг нь probabilistic equality гэдгийг үргэлж ялга.

blocks.text: Prefix recurrence-ийг задлавал $h_r$ нь $c_0B^{r-1}+\cdots+c_{r-1}$ гэсэн polynomial-ийн үлдэгдэл. $h_lB^{r-l}$ нь эхний $l$ тэмдэгтийн яг тэр зэрэгтэй хэсэг тул хасахад зөвхөн substring-ийн polynomial үлдэнэ.

Ижил substring-үүд заавал ижил hash-тай. Харин өөр string-үүд modulo авсны дараа давхцаж болно: хязгааргүй олон string-ийг хязгаартай тоон утгад буулгаж байгаа. Хоёр modulo collision-ийг багасгах боловч боломжгүй болгохгүй. Тогтмол base дээр дурын adversarial input-д баталгаатай магадлал зарлаж болохгүй.

Prefix болон power-уудыг байгуулахад тэмдэгт бүрд тогтмол ажил хийдэг тул $O(n)$. Query бүр хэдхэн arithmetic үйлдэлтэй $O(1)$; нийт $O(n+q)$. Хоёр modulo ашигласан нь тогтмол үржүүлэгч болохоос asymptotic bound-ийг өөрчлөхгүй.
Хоёр prefix, хоёр power vector нийлээд $O(n)$ space. Query бүрт substring-ийг substr-аар хуулбал hash хурдан байсан ч хуулбарлах $O(length)$ ажил нэмэгдэнэ.

items: MOD1, MOD2, BASE нь hash-ийн parameter; long long нь үржүүлэх үеийн завсрын утгыг багтаана.
$p_i=B^i\bmod M$, $h_i$ нь эхний $i$ тэмдэгтийн hash.
Хасалтын дараа MOD нэмээд % MOD авах нь сөрөг үлдэгдлийг normalize хийнэ.

Урт шалгахгүй байх, prefix index-д $l$ ба $l-1$-ийг андуурах.

tutorials.title: Loop invariant — кодын дунд юу үнэн хэвээр вэ?
tutorials.summary: Хоёр заагийн жишээгээр initialization, maintenance, termination гурвыг ялгаж баталгаа бичье.
tutorials.aliases: invariant Loop invariant — кодын дунд юу үнэн хэвээр вэ? Loop invariants — what stays true during the loop?

en.title: Loop invariants — what stays true during the loop?
en.summary: Use a two-pointer example to separate initialization, maintenance and termination.

blocks.text: Passing several examples does not establish correctness for every input. A loop invariant describes what remains true during execution, allowing us to justify why the next update is safe.

sections.title: 2. From the direct approach to the insight

blocks.text: Find two distinct indices summing to $X$ in a sorted array. Enumerating pairs costs $O(n^2)$. Compare the leftmost $l$ and rightmost $r$ values. The essential argument is why an entire boundary can safely be discarded.
Invariant: every not-yet-discarded possible solution has both indices in $[l,r]$. This does not claim a solution exists; it says we have not discarded any possible solution.
For $a=[1,2,4,6,8]$ and $X=10$, first $1+8=9<X$. The value $1$ cannot reach $10$ with any remaining partner, so increment $l$. Then $2+8=10$ finds a solution.

items: Initialize $l=0$, $r=n-1$.
While $l<r$, compute the sum and return a match.
Move $l$ inward if the sum is too small, or $r$ inward if it is too large.
If the boundaries meet, no pair of distinct remaining indices exists.

blocks.text: Initialization: $[0,n-1]$ contains all indices. Maintenance: if $a_l+a_r<X$, then every $j\le r$ satisfies $a_l+a_j\le a_l+a_r<X$, so no remaining solution uses $l$. Symmetrically, if the sum is too large, every $i\ge l$ gives $a_i+a_r>X$, so $r$ cannot belong to a remaining solution.
Termination: every update decreases $r-l$ by one. A reported pair sums to the target and has distinct indices because $l<r$. If $l\ge r$, the invariant leaves no possible pair of distinct indices.

sections.title: 6. Where the running time comes from

blocks.text: The initial boundary distance is $n-1$ and shrinks every iteration, giving $O(n)$ iterations of constant work. Extra search space is $O(1)$; the input array takes $O(n)$ space.

items: The input is promised sorted; sorting it yourself adds $O(n\log n)$ time.
Long long prevents overflow when summing the two input values.
The condition $l<r$ prevents reusing one index twice.
The printed one-based indices refer to positions in the sorted input.

blocks.text: $1\le n\le2\cdot10^5$, sorted array, $|a_i|\le10^9$. Read $n,X$ and the array. Print a pair of indices or -1 -1.

items: Assuming the final answer as part of the invariant you are supposed to prove.
Proving preservation but forgetting termination.
Using the inequalities on unsorted values.

blocks.text: Ask three questions for every new loop: why is the claim initially true, why does an update preserve it, and what does it imply at termination? The invariant differs for sorting, binary search, BFS, greedy or DP, but this structure remains the same.
Why is there no answer for $a=[5]$ and $X=10$?
Remember that the indices must be distinct.
blocks.label: Hint

blocks.text: One index cannot be used twice. The $l<r$ loop does not run.
blocks.label: Show explanation

blocks.text: Код хэдэн жишээн дээр зөв ажилласан ч бүх input дээр зөв гэдэг нь хараахан батлагдахгүй. Loop-ийн дунд ямар мэдээлэл зөв хэвээр байгааг тодорхойлбол дараагийн update яагаад аюулгүйг тайлбарлаж чадна. Үүнийг loop invariant гэдэг.

Sorted array-аас нийлбэр нь $X$ болох хоёр өөр index хайя. Бүх хос $O(n^2)$. Хамгийн зүүн $l$, хамгийн баруун $r$-ийг авч $a_l+a_r$-ийг $X$-тэй харьцуулна. Яагаад нэг заагийг бүхэлд нь хасаж болохыг батлах нь алгоритмын гол хэсэг.
Invariant: одоогоор хасаагүй бүх боломжит шийдлийн хоёр index $[l,r]$ дотор байна. Үлдсэн мужид шийдэл заавал байна гэж хэлээгүй; байж болох шийдлийг хасахгүй гэдгийг л хадгалж байгаа.
$a=[1,2,4,6,8]$, $X=10$. Эхлээд $1+8=9<X$, тиймээс $1$ ямар ч үлдсэн утгатай нийлээд $10$ болохгүй. $l$-ийг нэмэхэд $2+8=10$, хариу олдоно.

items: $l=0$, $r=n-1$ гэж эхэл.
$l<r$ үед нийлбэрийг олж тэнцүү бол хариул.
Нийлбэр бага бол $l$-ийг, их бол $r$-ийг дотогш шилжүүл.
Заагууд уулзвал хоёр өөр index үлдээгүй тул боломжгүй гэж шийд.

blocks.text: Initialization: эхэнд $[0,n-1]$ бүх index-ийг хамарсан тул invariant үнэн. Maintenance: $a_l+a_r<X$ бол $j\le r$ бүх $j$ дээр $a_l+a_j\le a_l+a_r<X$, тиймээс $l$-тэй бүх хос боломжгүй. Эсрэг тохиолдолд $i\ge l$ бүх $i$ дээр $a_i+a_r>X$ тул $r$-тэй бүх хос боломжгүй.
Termination: алхам бүр $r-l$-ийг нэгээр багасгана. Хариу олдсон бол нийлбэр тэнцүү, $l<r$ учраас хоёр index өөр. $l\ge r$ бол invariant-ийн дагуу байж болох ямар ч өөр index-ийн хос үлдээгүй.
Заагуудын хоорондын зай эхэнд $n-1$, алхам бүрд багасна. Иймээс хамгийн ихдээ $O(n)$ iteration, iteration бүр $O(1)$ ажилтай. Нэмэлт зай $O(1)$; input array $O(n)$.

items: Input sorted гэж өгөгдсөн. Өөрөө sort хийх бол $O(n\log n)$ хугацаа нэмж тооц.

Хэвлэхдээ $1$ нэмсэн index нь sorted input дээрх байрлал.

items: Invariant-даа яг батлах гэж байгаа эцсийн хариугаа урьдчилан үнэн гэж тавих.

tutorials.title: Counterexample ба stress testing
tutorials.summary: Жижиг зөв oracle, deterministic random generator, хамгийн жижиг алдаатай input-ээр кодоо шалгая.
tutorials.aliases: debugging Counterexample ба stress testing Counterexamples and stress testing

en.title: Counterexamples and stress testing
en.summary: Use a small exact oracle, reproducible random generation and small failing cases.

blocks.text: Randomly editing code that passes samples but fails hidden tests can introduce more errors. First obtain a small reproducible input and its correct answer. Stress testing compares the fast solution with a small, slow, clearly correct oracle.

sections.title: 2. From the direct approach to the insight

blocks.text: For maximum subarray sum, write an $O(n^2)$ oracle enumerating all interval sums. The fast candidate uses Kadane's recurrence. With small $n$, both are quick enough to compare automatically on many inputs.

A fixed random seed makes failures reproducible. Begin with targeted cases such as $n=1$, all-negative values and equal values rather than relying only on randomness. Temporarily introducing a known candidate bug checks whether the harness really detects it.
When the subarray must be nonempty, $[-5,-2]$ has answer $-2$. A buggy candidate initialized with best value zero may return zero; the small oracle exposes the mismatch immediately.

items: Read the statement and constraints again, then generate only valid inputs.
Keep the oracle simple and clearly correct rather than optimizing it.
On a mismatch, print the input, expected and actual results, then stop.
Shrink a failing input by removing elements or simplifying values.
After fixing it, retain the counterexample as a regression test.

blocks.text: The oracle examines every nonempty interval once and takes the maximum, establishing its result on small inputs. A mismatch proves at least one implementation is wrong; this is why the oracle itself must be checked.

Agreement on a thousand tests is not a proof for every input. Test unseen structures, large-input overflow, recursion depth and time limits separately. Stress testing is a bug-finding tool, not a replacement for a correctness argument.

sections.title: 6. Where the running time comes from

blocks.text: One oracle run costs $O(n^2)$ and the candidate costs $O(n)$. Across $T$ tests this is $O(Tn^2)$, so generated $n$ stays small. Do not run the oracle on production-sized inputs.
Both functions read the array by reference and use constant extra state. The harness stores its generated input in $O(n)$ space.

blocks.text: Sample дээр зөв боловч hidden test дээр буруу кодыг таамгаар өөрчилсөөр байвал шинэ алдаа нэмэх амархан. Алдааг дахин гаргаж чаддаг жижиг input болон түүн дээрх зөв хариу хэрэгтэй. Stress testing нь хурдан шийдлийг жижиг, удаан боловч ойлгомжтой oracle-тай харьцуулдаг.

Maximum subarray sum-ийг бүх $[l,r]$ завсрын нийлбэрийг тооцож $O(n^2)$ олох oracle бичье. Хурдан candidate нь Kadane-ийн recurrence. Жижиг $n$ дээр хоёулаа хурдан тул олон input-ийн хариуг автоматаар харьцуулж болно.

Генераторын seed-ийг тогтмол байлгавал олдсон алдаа дахин гарна. Зөвхөн random бус, $n=1$, бүх утга сөрөг, бүх утга ижил зэрэг чиглэсэн тестийг эхэлж оруул. Candidate-ийг санаатай буруу болгож шалгахад harness чинь алдааг үнэхээр барьж байгаа эсэх мэдэгдэнэ.
Хоосон subarray зөвшөөрөөгүй бодлогод $[-5,-2]$-ын хариу $-2$. Хэрэв best-ийг $0$-оос эхэлсэн буруу candidate $0$ гэвэл жижиг oracle зөрүүг шууд олно.

en.title: Subtask-oriented thinking and meet-in-the-middle
en.summary: Start with exact small-constraint solutions and distinguish the ranges where each method fits.

blocks.text: An IOI-style task may offer useful subtasks even before the full solution is clear. Read each subtask's constraints, required interface and scoring rules separately. We will use a training subset-sum example without inventing official point values.
Choose nonnegative weights with the largest subset sum at most $K$. Exhaustive search fits around $n\le20$. Small $K$ suggests DP, while $n\le40$ with large $K$ suggests meet-in-the-middle.

sections.title: 2. From the direct approach to the insight

blocks.text: Instead of examining $2^{40}$ subsets, split the input into halves of about $20$. Each half produces roughly $2^{20}$ subset sums. Every original subset corresponds to one pair: a left subset and a right subset.

Sort the right sums. For every left sum $x$, find the largest right sum at most $K-x$, immediately before upper bound. Checking every pair of the two lists directly would bring the work back to $2^n$.
Split $[6,4,3,2]$, $K=10$ into $[6,4]$ and $[3,2]$. Left sums are $[0,6,4,10]$ and sorted right sums $[0,2,3,5]$. For $x=6$ choose right sum $3$ to obtain $9$; for $x=10$ choose zero to obtain $10$.

items: Include the empty-subset sum zero in each list.
For each new weight, append versions of the previously existing sums with that weight added.
Nonnegative weights allow sums above $K$ to be discarded.
Sort the right list and binary search its best complement for each left sum.
Take the largest feasible combined sum.

blocks.text: When adding a weight, retain old subsets without it and append those old subsets with it. This covers every subset sum. Nonnegativity ensures a sum above $K$ cannot later decrease into a valid one.

Every optimal subset splits across the two halves. When its left sum $x$ is considered, the algorithm chooses the largest valid right sum, never a worse complement than the optimal subset's. All reported sums are feasible, so the global maximum is exact.

sections.title: 6. Where the running time comes from

blocks.text: Each half has $O(2^{n/2})$ subset sums. Iterative doubling generates them in time linear in the list size. Sorting and complement queries give $O(n2^{n/2})$ worst-case time and $O(2^{n/2})$ space.
At $n=40$ the two lists can contain a few million long long values; at $n=60$ they are already too large. Do not apply a method from one subtask mechanically to the full constraints.

items: Save the list size before adding a weight; do not reuse newly appended elements during that same iteration.
After sorting right sums, upper_bound finds the first value greater than $K-x$.
If the iterator equals begin, no preceding element exists; otherwise step back for the complement.
Do not copy this stdin program unchanged into an IOI task; follow the official grader function signature.

blocks.text: IOI-style бодлогод full solution шууд харагдахгүй байсан ч statement-ийн subtasks дээр ажиллаж болно. Subtask бүрийн constraint, шаардсан interface, онооны дүрмийг тусад нь унш. Энд албан бодлогын оноо зохиохгүй, нэг сургалтын subset sum жишээгээр алгоритмаа constraint-аас сонгоно.
Өгөгдсөн nonnegative жингүүдээс нийлбэр нь $K$-аас ихгүй хамгийн их subset sum ол. $n\le20$ үед бүх subset тоочиж болно. $K$ жижиг бол DP, харин $n\le40$, $K$ том үед meet-in-the-middle тохирч болно.

Бүх $2^{40}$ subset-ийг үзэхийн оронд input-ийг хоёр $20$ орчим урттай хэсэгт хуваа. Хэсэг тус бүрийн бүх subset sum-ийг гаргахад $2^{20}$ орчим утга л үүснэ. Original subset бүр зүүн subset, баруун subset гэсэн ганц хослолтой.
Баруун sums-ийг sort хийгээд зүүн sum $x$ бүрд $K-x$-аас ихгүй хамгийн их баруун sum хай. Upper bound-ийн өмнөх утга хэрэгтэй. Хоёр list-ийн бүх хосыг шууд шалгавал дахин $2^n$ ажил болно.
$[6,4,3,2]$, $K=10$-ийг $[6,4]$, $[3,2]$ гэж хуваа. Зүүн sums $[0,6,4,10]$, баруун sums $[0,2,3,5]$. $x=6$ үед $4$-өөс ихгүй хамгийн том баруун sum $3$, нийлбэр $9$; $x=10$ үед $0$ сонгож нийт $10$.

items: Хоосон subset-ийн $0$ нийлбэрийг list бүрд оруул.

blocks.text: Нэг хэсгийн sums үүсгэхдээ шинэ жинтэй subset-үүдийг хуучин subset дээр тэр жинг нэмж, жингүй subset-үүдийг хэвээр үлдээнэ. Ингэснээр бүх subset sum хамрагдана. Nonnegative учраас нэгэнт $K$-аас их болсон sum дахин valid болж буурахгүй.

Ямар ч optimal subset хоёр хэсэгтээ хуваагдана. Түүний зүүн sum $x$-ийг үзэхэд algorithm баруун талын бүх valid sum-ээс хамгийн ихийг сонгодог тул optimal баруун sum-ээс дор сонголт хийхгүй. Гаргасан бүх нийлбэр $K$-аас ихгүй тул нийт maximum яг optimum.

Нэг хэсгийн subset-үүд $O(2^{n/2})$ хэмжээтэй. List-ийг iterative doubling-оор үүсгэх нийт ажил тэдний хэмжээнд linear. Sort болон complement query-уудыг нэмээд worst-case $O(n2^{n/2})$ хугацаа, $O(2^{n/2})$ зай.
$n=40$ үед хоёр list нийт хэдэн сая long long хадгалж болно; $n=60$ бол энэ ч хэт том. Нэг subtask-д ажилласан алгоритмаа full constraints дээр механикаар хэрэглэхгүй.
